recommendation.presentation: Use Turing as the initial opening quotation, with a compact author/work/year attribution linked to the original text. If alternatives are included, let the reader switch them deliberately; do not auto-rotate text during reading. Use Leveson beside the investigation questions rather than crowding the opening. Remove the 832/11/27 showcase statistics.
recommendation.caution: These are historical quotations, not claims by the quoted authors about the 2026 incident. Keep factual incident description and evidence attribution separate.

quotations.quote: Machines take me by surprise with great frequency.
quotations.author: Alan Turing
quotations.locator: Original p. 450; section 6, Contrary Views on the Main Question; objection (6), Lady Lovelace’s Objection. The sentence appears before the p. 451 marker in the MSU transcription.
quotations.exactness: Complete sentence, capitalization and wording unchanged.
quotations.source_type: Full primary paper, hosted by Michigan State University; wording corroborated in the Brooklyn College primary-text PDF.
quotations.context: Turing replies to the claim that a machine cannot surprise us. He describes how incomplete calculations and forgotten assumptions produce unexpected behavior, rather than treating surprise as proof of consciousness.
quotations.why_it_fits: The strongest opening: brief, wry, immediately understandable, and directly relevant to the gap between expected and observed machine behavior. It creates curiosity without prejudging the incident’s cause.

quotations.quote: We must always exert the full strength of our imagination to examine where the full use of our new modalities may lead us.
quotations.author: Norbert Wiener
quotations.work: Some Moral and Technical Consequences of Automation
quotations.publication: Science, New Series, volume 131, number 3410, pp. 1355–1358
quotations.locator: Printed p. 1358, PDF page 5, closing part of the Time Scales section. Sentence follows the warning against assuming that faster adoption of new powers is necessarily better.
quotations.exactness: Complete sentence, with only PDF line wrapping removed.
quotations.source_type: Scan of the original Science article, hosted by Penn State.
quotations.context: Wiener discusses the mismatch between human and machine timescales, incomplete communication of purposes, and the difficulty of judging the consequences of newly available capabilities.
quotations.why_it_fits: An expansive, constructive counterpoint to the incident: investigation is useful because it helps examine where powerful tools can lead. It also connects naturally to anticipatory analysis.

quotations.quote: For a successful technology, reality must take precedence over public relations, for nature cannot be fooled.
quotations.author: Richard P. Feynman
quotations.work: Personal Observations on Reliability of Shuttle
quotations.publication: Report of the Presidential Commission on the Space Shuttle Challenger Accident, volume 2, appendix F
quotations.locator: Conclusions, last sentence, printed p. F5.
quotations.exactness: Complete sentence, preserving NASA’s lowercase nature.
quotations.source_type: NASA’s primary publication of Feynman’s commission appendix.
quotations.context: Feynman contrasts engineering evidence with managerial reliability claims, examines certification practices and communication gaps, and calls for realistic assessment of technological limitations.
quotations.why_it_fits: The sharpest investigation-focused alternative. Memorable and tightly connected to evidence quality and institutional assumptions. Its sharper tone should not be used to imply that a particular organization’s deception has been established.

quotations.quote: Some accident investigators have actually complained that CAST creates too much information about the causes of a loss.
quotations.author: Nancy G. Leveson
quotations.work: CAST Handbook: How to Learn More from Incidents and Accidents
quotations.locator: Printed p. 7, PDF page 7, Chapter 1, What is CAST?, final paragraph continuing onto printed p. 8.
quotations.exactness: Complete sentence, with only PDF line wrapping removed.
quotations.source_type: Author’s original handbook, hosted by MIT’s Partnership for Systems Approaches to Safety and Security.
quotations.context: Leveson rejects stopping at an arbitrary root cause and argues for learning extensively from each loss. She follows this sentence by questioning whether a simple explanation should be the goal.
quotations.why_it_fits: A pointed, surprising line that matches the user’s demand for maximal additional information. Best placed at the entrance to the CAST inquiry or evidence-collection section, where the research must substantiate the ambition.
quotations.recommended_use: Contextual quotation within CAST inquiry, not another opening statistic
